cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend: Jacob and his whole family are living in Egypt now, in the region of Goshen. Jacob's son Joseph is second only to Pharaoh here (Genesis 41:40-41). God renamed Jacob Israel (Genesis 32:28), so you'll hear both names, and his family is called the Israelites.

cards.question: The Israelites are settled in Goshen. How do they do there?

answers.text: They gain property and grow greatly in number
They lose their flocks and scatter across Egypt
They pack up and head back to Canaan

cards.text: Jacob lives in Egypt seventeen years, and the length of his life is 147 years. ONE HUNDRED FORTY-SEVEN, friend, and I thought my years in the back of a junk drawer felt long!
Then the time draws near for Israel to die, and he calls in his son Joseph with a request about where he'll be buried.

cards.question: Jacob asks Joseph to put his hand under his thigh and promise to show him kindness and faithfulness. What does Jacob want him to promise?

answers.text: Carry him out of Egypt to be buried with his fathers
Bury him in Goshen among his people
Bury him wherever Joseph thinks is best

cards.question: Joseph answers that he'll do as his father asked. True or false: Jacob takes his word for it and asks for nothing more.

cards.text: Jacob says, "Swear to me," and this man wants it SWORN, friend, no handshake deals. So Joseph swears.

cards.question: True or false: Once Joseph swears, Israel bows in worship at the head of his bed.

cards.text: Some time later, Joseph gets word: "Your father is ill." So he sets out with his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.

cards.question: True or false: When Jacob is told that Joseph has come, he's too weak to even sit up.

cards.text: Israel rallies his strength and sits UP in bed, like me hopping to attention when the oven timer dings. Then he tells Joseph that God Almighty appeared to him at Luz, in the land of Canaan, blessed him, and told him He would make him fruitful and multiply him.

cards.question: At Luz, God also said He would give the land to Jacob's ___ after him as an everlasting possession.

cards.text: Now Jacob turns to the subject of Joseph's two boys, the ones born to Joseph in Egypt before Jacob came. And what he says about them is BIG, friend.

cards.question: What does Jacob say about Ephraim and Manasseh, Joseph's two boys born in Egypt?

answers.text: They will be counted as his own sons
They will serve their uncles in Canaan
They will stay behind in Pharaoh's house

cards.text: They're his, he says, just as Reuben and Simeon are his, and those are Jacob's two oldest sons (Genesis 29:32-33). The grandsons just got moved up a whole branch on the family tree!

cards.question: True or false: Jacob says any children Joseph has after these two will be Joseph's own.

cards.text: Then Jacob talks about Rachel, his wife and Joseph's mother (Genesis 29:28; 30:22-24). On the way back from Paddan, to his sorrow, she died along the way in the land of Canaan.

cards.question: Rachel died along the way in Canaan. Where did Jacob bury her?

cards.text: Israel sees Joseph's sons and asks, "Who are these?" Joseph tells him they're the sons God has given him in this place.

cards.question: Jacob asks Joseph to bring the boys to him so he can bless them. True or false: Jacob can see Joseph's boys clearly when they come to him.

cards.text: Israel's eyesight is poor from old age, so poor he can hardly see. Joseph brings the boys close, and his father kisses and embraces them.

cards.question: Holding the boys, Israel tells Joseph he never expected to see his face again, but now God has let him see Joseph's ___ as well.

cards.text: Then Joseph takes his sons off his father's knees and bows facedown. He lines them up with Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel's left, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel's right.

cards.question: Manasseh is Joseph's firstborn (Genesis 41:51-52), and he's lined up with Israel's right hand. What does Israel do?

answers.text: He crosses his hands and puts his right on Ephraim
He puts his right hand on Manasseh's head
He has Joseph swap the two boys around

cards.text: Then Israel blesses Joseph. He calls on the God his grandfather Abraham and his father Isaac walked before (Genesis 25:19-26), "the God who has been my shepherd all my life to this day, the angel who has redeemed me from all harm…"

cards.question: Calling on the God who has been his shepherd all his life, Israel says may He bless Joseph's ___.
Israel also says may the boys grow into a multitude upon the earth. True or false: he says may they be called by his name and the names of Abraham and Isaac.

cards.text: But Joseph sees his father's right hand on Ephraim's head, and he is displeased. He takes his father's hand to move it over to Manasseh's head, like a man straightening a crooked picture frame in somebody else's house.

cards.question: As Joseph takes his father's hand to move it, what does he tell him?

answers.text: This one is the firstborn so put your right hand on him
Your eyes are tired so let me guide your hands
Ephraim is too young so bless him another day

cards.question: True or false: Israel lets Joseph move his right hand over to Manasseh.

cards.text: His father refuses: "I know, my son, I know!" Not one "I know," friend, TWO, and that's a man who knows EXACTLY where his hands are.

cards.question: Israel says Manasseh will become a people and be great too. So what does he say about Ephraim, the younger brother?

answers.text: He'll be greater and his offspring will become many nations
He'll serve Manasseh for the rest of his life
He'll lead the whole family back to Canaan

cards.text: So that day Jacob blesses them, and he says his people Israel will pronounce a blessing by them.

cards.question: What blessing does Jacob say his people Israel will pronounce by Joseph's two boys?

answers.text: May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh
May God keep you as He kept Joseph
May God bless you as He blessed Jacob

cards.text: So he puts Ephraim before Manasseh. Younger brother, FIRST in line, friend, that's the new hire walking into the corner office!

cards.question: Israel tells Joseph he's about to die. True or false: he also says God will be with Joseph and bring him back to the land of his fathers.
Last, Israel gives Joseph, as one above his brothers, something he took with his sword and bow from the Amorites, a people of Canaan (Genesis 10:15-16). What is it?

cards.text: We'll let this batch cool right here, friend. This family's story keeps on going.
